prompt: Most people are now aware of the environmental damage caused by air travel, yet the number of flights taken each year continues to rise. Why do people keep flying? What should be done about this?
essay:
There is no shortage of awareness about aviation and the climate; there is a shortage of reasons for any individual to act on it. That is not hypocrisy. It is what happens when the cost of a decision is spread across the entire planet while its benefit lands entirely on the person making it.

Two features of the market make flying almost irresistible. The first is that its price is fictitious. Kerosene is untaxed by international agreement, tickets are typically exempt from the sales taxes applied to nearly everything else, and the resulting fare covers the airline's costs while omitting the atmosphere's. A traveller comparing a fifty-pound flight with a ninety-pound train fare is not being wicked; they are reading a price that has had the damage deleted from it.

The second is that the alternative behaviour is invisible, including to the person performing it. Declining to fly produces nothing — no seat is removed, no aircraft is cancelled, nobody notices — while the reasons to go are vivid and personal: a grandparent on another continent, a week of sunlight after a long winter. Any argument that pits a diffuse, delayed and shared cost against a concrete, immediate and private benefit will lose, and it will keep losing however well it is made.

The remedy follows directly. If the problem is a distorted price, correct the price: tax aviation fuel as other fuels are taxed, and structure the charge so that it escalates with each flight an individual takes within a year, which places the burden on the small minority who fly repeatedly rather than on the family that goes abroad once. Then spend the proceeds making rail genuinely cheaper than flying on routes under a few hundred miles. Do that and the appeal to conscience becomes unnecessary, because the convenient choice and the responsible one finally coincide.
title: Why people keep flying despite the climate cost
